clue.text: Clear fortune, almost, I had

indicators.note: almost means the word for fortune stops one letter short of its full length

parts.note: fortune means luck
I had contracts to I'd, written ID

explanation.surface: A gambler admits plainly that their luck very nearly held.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucid explanation is a clear, easily understood one, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: It provides openings for otherwise excluded children

definitions.text: It provides openings for otherwise excluded children

parts.words: It provides openings for otherwise excluded children
parts.note: describes the door key worn by children who come home from school to an empty house and would otherwise be locked out

explanation.definitionFit: Latchkey children carry their own front door key because no parent is home when school ends.

clue.text: In election period, party had to straighten out Left

parts.note: a camp is a faction or party

indicators.note: out means the letter for Left is thrown out of the verb for straighten

parts.note: to align is to straighten into line

explanation.surface: During the run-up to an election, the party had to sort out its left wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a political wing, but it is just the letter L dropped from ALIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign is the organised period of canvassing before an election.

clue.text: Sell a lot of lions?

parts.note: a merchant of big cats would literally trade in creatures that roar, while the idiom means to sell briskly

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to do brisk business, selling large quantities, here read literally with roaring beasts.

clue.text: Brown enters compelling relationship

indicators.note: enters means one piece goes inside the other, here the colour inside the adjective

parts.note: a compelling argument is a cogent one
tan is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: A man named Brown embarks on an irresistible love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a surname and 'relationship' like romance, but the definition is mathematical.
explanation.definitionFit: In trigonometry the cotangent is one of the standard ratio relationships between an angle and the sides of a right triangle.

clue.text: Low-lying islands always covered in nasty gas

indicators.note: covered in means the word for always is wrapped by the gas's letters

parts.note: CS gas is a tear gas used in riot control
ay, also spelt aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Small islands are constantly shrouded in noxious fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: AY is an archaic or poetic word for 'always'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cays are small low islands formed of sand or coral, also called keys.

clue.text: Ordering shortly to tuck into doughnuts and pasta

indicators.note: to tuck into means the shortened ordering word is placed inside the doughnuts

parts.note: tori is the plural of torus, the geometric doughnut shape

indicators.note: shortly means the word for ordering loses its final letter

parts.note: telling someone to do something is ordering them

explanation.surface: Someone orders, curtly, to dig into the doughnuts and the pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doughnuts' is the mathematical sense: TORI, plural of torus. TELLIN is TELLING cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortellini are small ring-shaped stuffed pasta parcels from northern Italy.

clue.text: Calculating how many are taking cereal?

parts.note: a number answers the question how many
eating crisp breakfast cereal is crunching it

explanation.surface: Counting how many people are eating their breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is a link; read playfully, a number of people are crunching cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Number-crunching is slang for heavy calculation, especially processing large amounts of data.

clue.text: Worry about bishop's article showing mistakes

indicators.note: about means the worry word goes round the bishop's letters

parts.note: to eat at someone is to worry them, as in what's eating you
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Anxiety about a bishop's written piece reveals some errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worry' is EAT as in 'What's eating you?'; RR (Right Reverend) is a bishop's style.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed errors in a printed book, the plural of erratum.

clue.text: Teachers' noises of disapproval about men

definitions.note: the possessive apostrophe is surface dressing: the answer is the plain plural, people who teach

indicators.note: about means the disapproving noises go round the soldiers

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound of disapproval
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Teachers make disapproving tutting sounds about the men.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is military shorthand for enlisted men.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutors are private teachers or university staff who teach small groups.

clue.text: American boy's rude call to Godiva?

definitions.meaning: Mark Twain's famous boy hero from Missouri
Peeping Tom spied on Lady Godiva riding naked through Coventry; a cheeky shout of 'Tom saw you!' in dialect would say it

explanation.surface: A boy from the States shouts something cheeky at a naked lady on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Godiva rode naked through Coventry; Peeping Tom was the man who looked. 'Saw yer' is a casual spelling of 'saw you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain's novel makes this name the archetypal American boy of the Mississippi river towns.

clue.text: Worth replacing exhaust at end of motorway

indicators.note: at end of means the rearranged piece is placed after the motorway letter

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: replacing read as re-placing, putting the letters of the verb for exhaust in a new order

parts.note: to exhaust someone is to tire them

explanation.surface: Is it worthwhile swapping the car's exhaust pipe when you reach the end of the motorway?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust' looks like a car part but is the verb TIRE; 'replacing' rearranges it to ERIT, which goes at the end of M.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit and worth are synonyms for the value or quality something has.

clue.text: Sensibly keep this screwed, avoiding flinching

definitions.meaning: a sensible person is said to have their head screwed on
facing a problem directly, without dodging, is meeting it full-frontally

explanation.surface: Advice on keeping a screw tight and not wincing while you do it.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into a noun and adverb: the thing a sensible person keeps screwed on.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct, unflinching confrontation is called a head-on one, facing the issue squarely.

clue.text: Guardsman dropping fine bird

indicators.note: dropping means one letter is let fall out of the guardsman's name

parts.note: a Beefeater is a Yeoman Warder guarding the Tower of London
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: A soldier on guard duty lets slip a fine bird he spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: A Beefeater is one of the ceremonial guards at the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The bee-eater is a brightly coloured bird that catches bees and wasps in flight.

clue.text: Tart collection of asperities bandied about

indicators.note: bandied about means the letters are tossed around into a new order

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued woman gathers up harsh words and throws them around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' suggests sharpness, like the asperities, but here it is a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Patisserie means pastries and cakes collectively, including a baker's array of tarts.

clue.text: Author's rework a wag recalled

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: to rework something is to remake it, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer's revision of what a joker once remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rework' rearranges the twelve letters of 'a wag recalled'. Edgar Wallace was a prolific British thriller writer of the early twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Wallace was a British novelist, creator of King Kong's screenplay and countless crime thrillers.

clue.text: Cast in series fail to catch fire

indicators.note: in means the cast is placed inside the abbreviation for series

parts.note: a cast is a mould, as for metal or plaster

explanation.surface: Actors in a TV series fail to ignite any spark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like actors but is a noun for a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: To smoulder is to burn slowly with smoke but no flame, never quite catching fire.

clue.text: Invoice broke poor farm

indicators.note: broke is read as broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bill bankrupted a struggling farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' looks like 'penniless', fitting the poor farm, but signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro forma is a preliminary invoice sent ahead of goods or payment.

clue.text: Welcome warmth from counter-wallah

parts.note: wallah is a word of Indian origin for a person in charge of something, so it points to India
read whimsically, a counter is one who sums, a summer

explanation.surface: A shop worker behind a counter gives a cheerful, warm greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter-wallah' looks like a shop assistant; read as an Indian 'summer' (one who sums), it gives the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian summer is a spell of unexpectedly warm weather in autumn, always a pleasant surprise.

clue.text: Splendid welcome not right for resistance leader

indicators.note: not right means the letter for right is removed

parts.note: grand means splendid or magnificent
hi is a word of welcome

explanation.surface: A magnificent welcome would be wrong for a rebel chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resistance' is passive resistance: Gandhi led India's non-violent independence movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi led India's non-violent resistance movement against British rule.

clue.text: Fragments of law

definitions.meaning: a picture assembled from small fragments of stone or glass
relating to Moses, the lawgiver of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Pieces of legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mosaic law is the law of Moses in the first books of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosaic is built from fragments, and Mosaic law is the law given through Moses.

clue.text: Write down a suggestion almost entirely in code

indicators.note: in means the shortened suggestion sits inside the code's name

parts.note: Morse is the dot-and-dash code

indicators.note: almost entirely means all of the word for suggestion except its last letter

parts.note: a tip is a helpful suggestion

explanation.surface: Someone notes a hint that has been written almost completely in cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Write down' is the accountant's sense, reducing a debt or asset's value over time.
explanation.definitionFit: To amortise is to write off a cost or debt gradually, writing down its book value.

clue.text: Untidy person, say, needs collar

definitions.meaning: to collar someone is to grab them by the back of the neck

explanation.surface: A slovenly man needs a collar to smarten him up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collar' looks like a shirt part but is the verb: to seize by the nape.
explanation.definitionFit: Scruff names both a shabby person and the nape of the neck, by which one is grabbed.

clue.text: Indecent talk almost finished the general

indicators.note: almost finished means the general's name stops short of its final letter

parts.note: Jan Smuts was a South African general and statesman

explanation.surface: Dirty talk nearly finished off the army commander.
explanation.walkthrough: Jan Smuts was a Boer general and later South African prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is obscene or indecent talk, writing or pictures.

clue.text: Show stuff concealed by attorney

indicators.note: concealed by means the verb for stuff is enclosed within the attorney's letters

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney in the US
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: A lawyer hides some material for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play or show performed on stage or screen.

clue.text: Scrap book

definitions.meaning: a scrap left over is what remains
in publishing, to ... a book is to sell off unsold copies cheaply

explanation.surface: An instruction to throw away a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' is a publisher's verb here: unsold stock is remaindered, sold off at a discount.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover scrap is a remainder, and remaindered books are surplus stock sold cheaply.

clue.text: Small addition in material for building across river

indicators.note: across means the building material spans, so encloses, the river letter

parts.note: cement is a building material
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A small extension to a house uses cement brought across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An increment is a small increase, such as a step up on a pay scale.

clue.text: Policeman backs a hunt

indicators.note: backs means the whole phrase is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a drag hunt follows an artificial scent laid by dragging a lure

explanation.surface: A police officer gives support to a fox hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' turns A DRAG round. A garda is an officer of the Irish police, the Garda Síochána.
explanation.definitionFit: Garda is the name for the Irish police force and also an individual officer in it.
